drug_class: Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor (EGFR) Inhibitor; Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitor

avoid_supplements.name: St. John's Wort
avoid_supplements.mechanism: P-glycoprotein inducer may increase afatinib efflux and reduce plasma concentrations
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concomitant use; consider alternative mood support if needed

avoid_supplements.name: Ginkgo biloba
avoid_supplements.mechanism: May potentiate bleeding risk and increase gastrointestinal side effects
avoid_supplements.action: Discontinue use or monitor closely for signs of bleeding

caution_supplements.name: Calcium and magnesium supplements
caution_supplements.mechanism: May reduce afatinib absorption if taken simultaneously; afatinib requires acidic pH for optimal absorption
caution_supplements.action: Separate dosing by at least 2 hours; take afatinib on empty stomach

caution_supplements.name: Iron supplements
caution_supplements.mechanism: May chelate afatinib and reduce bioavailability
caution_supplements.action: Space dosing at least 2 hours apart from afatinib

avoid_foods.name: High-fat meals
avoid_foods.mechanism: Significantly increases afatinib bioavailability (up to 39% increase), risking increased toxicity and adverse effects
avoid_foods.action: Take afatinib on an empty stomach; avoid fatty meals for 3 hours before and 1 hour after dosing

caution_foods.name: Dairy products and calcium-rich foods
caution_foods.mechanism: Calcium content may reduce afatinib absorption due to pH-dependent absorption mechanism
caution_foods.action: Separate intake by at least 2 hours from afatinib administration

caution_foods.name: Grapefruit and grapefruit juice
caution_foods.mechanism: Potential P-gp inhibition may affect afatinib disposition, though clinical significance is limited
caution_foods.action: Moderate consumption or consider alternative citrus fruits

monitoring_notes: Afatinib absorption is pH-dependent and significantly affected by food composition; consistent empty-stomach dosing is critical for optimal drug exposure. Monitor for gastrointestinal toxicity (diarrhea, nausea) and dermatologic reactions, as these are dose-dependent and may be exacerbated by high bioavailability states.
